summary: Clearwater NF lookout in Idaho County: tree platform from 1934 or 1935, 40-foot L-4 tower by 1946 or 1949, destroyed or removed in 1973; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 40-foot pole tower with L-4 cab, after an earlier tree platform
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1973 per three sources; Forest Lookouts, citing Kresek, says removed. No source describes what remains.

staffing.status: last manned by the Lochsa District in 1953; in use again by 1966 after transfer to the Powell District

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts tags the site as hike-in

events.note: 45-foot tree platform as first lookout; Hartig (source 3) dates the first manned season to 1935
First lookout manned at the start of the 1935 fire season, per Hartig's 1981 history; tent camp near larch topped at 55 feet
Ten feet cut off the tree top; crow's nest at 45 feet with wooden ladder
40-foot pole L-4 tower, per firelookout.com; Hartig dates the cab move to 1947 and construction funding to 1949
Construction of the 40-foot tower with L-4 cab begins after funding; George Brocke and family moved to the point
Last manned by the Lochsa District, then dropped from the fire plan
Transferred to the Powell District and activated again; still in use in 1966
Destroyed per firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Clearwater list
Forest Lookouts page, citing Kresek, says the lookout was removed; conflicts with destroyed

notes_for_editor: Conflicts: first lookout dated 1934 (sources 1, 2, 4) vs first manned 1935 (Hartig, source 3); tower dated 1946 (sources 1, 2, 4) vs construction funded 1949 (Hartig); destroyed 1973 (sources 1, 2, 4) vs removed 1973 (source 3). The Hartig history is quoted secondhand on the Forest Lookouts page (1981). A Waymarking page (wmFJK4_Mocus_Point_Trail_Bridge_Idaho) describes Trail #469 as a 4.9-mile route to 'a former fire lookout site', but the cached fetch returned only the title, so it is not quoted and not used. The brief's record says destroyed 1973, which matches sources 1, 2 and 4. No photo added: direct image URLs were not retrieved.
